question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Twin-plate barcoding to read out the pre-treatment state of future survivors
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal population, split it into twin plates so that each barcode is represented in both, treat one plate and deeply profile the untreated twin by scRNA-seq. Because survivors are identified retrospectively by barcode, this directly reveals the transcriptional state the surviving cells were in before they ever saw drug, rather than the post-hoc state of cells already reshaped by treatment.

ideas.title: Measure the memory half-life of the primed state
ideas.description: Sort cells that are in the putative primed state (by a FISH-based or reporter-based readout), re-plate them, and assay drug survival and marker expression at a series of time points as the sorted population relaxes back toward baseline. The decay curve gives a quantitative switching rate that distinguishes a transient transcriptional fluctuation from a stably heritable epigenetic state.

ideas.title: Fluctuation analysis of survivor counts to infer switching rates
ideas.description: Grow many small parallel cultures from few cells, treat each identically, and count survivor colonies per culture. The shape of the variance across cultures (Luria-Delbrück style) discriminates rare irreversible events arising early in the lineage from fast reversible state-switching, and yields switching and reversion rates without any molecular profiling.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome to test whether chromatin is primed before transcription
ideas.description: Perform joint ATAC and RNA profiling on untreated cells to ask whether the regulatory regions of resistance-associated genes are already accessible in cells that have not yet upregulated those transcripts. A population with open-but-silent chromatin would identify an intermediate, pre-primed compartment much larger than the eventual survivor fraction.

ideas.title: Spatial and conditioned-media tests for non-cell-autonomous survival
ideas.description: Image whether survivor colonies are spatially clustered more than expected by chance, and complement this with conditioned-media transfer and mixed co-culture of labeled sensitive cells. Together these separate genuinely cell-intrinsic priming from local paracrine protection or density effects, a confound rarely excluded in single-cell priming studies.

candidates: Clonal barcoding with split-sister-cell design: barcode a population, split into twin plates, treat one and profile the other to find pre-existing states that predict survival
Prospective isolation of rare high-expressor cells by RNA FISH-based sorting, then re-plating to test whether the state is heritable and drug-protective
Live-cell imaging with a fluorescent reporter knock-in at a resistance-associated locus to track state fluctuations and time-to-commitment before drug addition
Single-cell multiome (ATAC + RNA) of pre-treatment cells to ask whether primed chromatin precedes primed transcription
Timed drug-addition/removal experiments measuring the memory half-life of the primed state (how long before a sorted cell reverts)
Whole-genome and targeted deep sequencing of survivor colonies to rule in or out pre-existing mutations and copy-number changes
CRISPR screens for genes whose loss blocks the emergence of survivors without affecting bulk drug killing
Mitochondrial or metabolic single-cell measurements (mitochondrial mass, membrane potential, ROS) as a non-transcriptional predictor of survival
Cell-cycle phase at the moment of drug addition, measured by FUCCI live imaging, correlated with individual cell fate
Quantifying drug uptake and efflux per cell with fluorescent drug analogs or mass spectrometry imaging
Single-cell signaling dynamics (ERK/AKT kinase translocation reporters) during the first hours of drug exposure, linked to eventual fate
Measuring cell size, protein content, and global translation rate per cell as a confounder/predictor of survival
Spatial analysis of whether survivors arise in clusters, indicating local microenvironment or paracrine effects rather than cell-intrinsic state
Conditioned-media and co-culture swap experiments to test whether dying cells release factors that protect neighbors
Serial re-treatment of resistant colonies after drug holiday to measure reversibility and distinguish epigenetic from genetic resistance
Allele-specific and monoallelic expression analysis in single cells to test whether stochastic bursting at one allele creates rare high states
Perturbing transcriptional burst kinetics (e.g., with BET or HDAC modulators) and measuring the effect on survivor frequency
Single-cell proteomics or high-plex imaging of signaling proteins to check whether RNA-level priming is reflected at protein level
Mathematical inference of state-switching rates from fluctuation analysis (Luria-Delbrück style) applied to drug-survivor counts
Comparing survivor frequency and identity across isogenic subclones to quantify how much variability is clone-heritable versus truly stochastic
